repairs.failure_pattern: A pretrained transformer sequence-classification model raises TypeError during initialization because dropout-related settings are passed directly to from_pretrained even though the selected architecture accepts them only through its configuration.
repair_steps: Load the checkpoint configuration with AutoConfig.from_pretrained or the architecture-specific config class.
Set the dropout fields actually exposed by that configuration, such as classifier_dropout, hidden_dropout_prob, attention_probs_dropout_prob, dropout, or attention_dropout.
Instantiate the sequence-classification model with from_pretrained using the modified config and num_labels, without forwarding dropout fields as standalone constructor keywords.
Inspect or validate the selected configuration fields before starting cross-validation or full training.
repairs.root_cause: Dropout parameter names and constructor signatures vary across ModernBERT, DistilBERT, and RoBERTa implementations; configuration fields were incorrectly treated as universal model constructor arguments.
repairs.title: Confirmed: configure transformer dropout through the checkpoint configuration
repairs.when_to_use: Use when ModernBERT, DistilBERT, RoBERTa, or another Hugging Face sequence classifier fails before training with an unexpected dropout-related keyword argument.

repairs.failure_pattern: A text classifier combining SBERT, TF-IDF, pooled transformer, or projected representations fails on its first forward pass because a linear, branch, or recurrent layer expects a hardcoded width different from the actual feature width.
repair_steps: After fitting each feature extractor, read its actual output width from the resulting matrix or vectorizer vocabulary.
Pass semantic_dim, tfidf_dim, projection_dim, and other source dimensions explicitly into the model constructor.
Define each source projection with its source width, for example Linear(tfidf_dim, projection_dim), rather than deriving it from an unrelated hidden size.
Set downstream branch or recurrent input widths to the exact post-operation width: sum widths after concatenation and use the projected width after projection.
Add assertions before training that batch feature widths match their projection layers and that the fused tensor width matches every downstream branch.
repairs.root_cause: Feature dimensions were duplicated as constants in the model definition instead of being propagated from fitted vectorizers and encoder outputs; projection or concatenation changed the representation width without updating downstream layers.
repairs.title: Confirmed: derive every fusion-layer dimension from extracted feature tensors
repairs.when_to_use: Use when this author-classification pipeline combines variable-width TF-IDF or stylometric features with fixed-width sentence or transformer embeddings and reports a matrix-multiplication or recurrent input_size mismatch.

repairs.failure_pattern: Validation cross-entropy remains finite, but manually computed multiclass log loss becomes NaN after the classifier emits probabilities equal to zero or one.
repair_steps: Collect validation logits in evaluation mode and convert them to probabilities with a numerically stable softmax.
Clip probabilities to a fixed epsilon interval before any logarithm, for example [1e-15, 1 - 1e-15].
Renormalize every probability row after clipping so each row sums to one.
Compute multiclass log loss with a standard metric implementation and an explicit complete class-label ordering.
Reject non-finite metric values before checkpoint selection so NaN cannot be treated as an improvement.
repairs.root_cause: The metric takes logarithms before enforcing a finite probability range, so exact zero probabilities produce negative infinity and subsequent aggregation produces NaN.
repairs.title: Confirmed: clip and renormalize class probabilities before multiclass log loss
repairs.when_to_use: Use when validation predictions for EAP, HPL, and MWS are finite but manual log-loss evaluation becomes NaN as transformer training grows highly confident.

repairs.failure_pattern: Validation fails when a one-dimensional vector of integer class IDs is multiplied directly by the logarithm of an N-by-C probability matrix.
repair_steps: Keep validation targets as integer class indices and pass them with the N-by-C probability matrix to a multiclass log-loss implementation with explicit labels.
If a manual formula is required, convert class indices to an N-by-C one-hot matrix using the same class ordering as the model outputs.
Assert that the probability matrix has one column for each of EAP, HPL, and MWS and that target IDs are within that ordering.
Perform validation metric computation once per epoch from the complete accumulated targets and predictions.
repairs.root_cause: The manual metric formula assumes one-hot targets, but the validation loader supplies class indices, producing incompatible target and probability shapes.
repairs.title: Provisional: compute multiclass log loss from class indices with a compatible metric
repairs.when_to_use: Use when author labels have shape N, predicted probabilities have shape N-by-3, and validation crashes with a broadcasting error during log-loss calculation.

repairs.failure_pattern: Training reports a strong best validation log loss, but evaluation after reloading the supposed best model is substantially worse on the same validation split.
repair_steps: Capture the best checkpoint as a deep CPU clone of every state_dict tensor or save it immediately to a checkpoint file.
Store the associated epoch, validation indices, label ordering, tokenizer settings, and best metric alongside the weights.
Reload the saved state with strict key checking into the same model configuration.
Call model.eval and run the identical validation inference function used during epoch scoring, including the same softmax, clipping, and class ordering.
Verify immediately after reload that the recomputed score matches the recorded best score within numerical tolerance before generating test predictions.
repairs.root_cause: The retained best state or final evaluation path is not guaranteed to be an immutable, exact reproduction of the state and inference procedure used when the best score was recorded.
repairs.title: Provisional: preserve and reload an immutable best-checkpoint state
repairs.when_to_use: Use when early stopping identifies a best author-classification epoch but the final score on the unchanged validation split degrades sharply after checkpoint restoration.

repairs.failure_pattern: Loading a DeBERTa-v3 checkpoint through a DeBERTa-v1 model class produces an architecture warning followed by embedding or parameter size mismatches.
repair_steps: Load the checkpoint with AutoConfig and inspect its declared model_type.
Use AutoModel or AutoModelForSequenceClassification so the library selects the checkpoint-compatible DeBERTa implementation.
Build any custom classification head from the hidden size reported by the loaded configuration.
Perform a small tokenized forward-pass smoke test before beginning stratified cross-validation.
repairs.root_cause: The checkpoint declares a DeBERTa-v2/v3-compatible architecture, but the code forces construction through the incompatible DebertaModel class.
repairs.title: Provisional: match the model loader class to the checkpoint architecture
repairs.when_to_use: Use when microsoft/deberta-v3-base or another DeBERTa-v3 checkpoint warns that a deberta-v2 model is being instantiated as deberta and then reports parameter-size mismatches.

repairs.failure_pattern: The first mixed-precision forward pass fails because attention scores in float16 are masked with a large negative constant such as -1e9 that cannot be represented by the tensor dtype.
repair_steps: Determine the attention score tensor dtype inside the pooling forward pass.
Replace the fixed -1e9 sentinel with a representable dtype-aware value such as torch.finfo(scores.dtype).min, or compute masking and softmax in float32.
Apply the padding mask before softmax and ensure each sample retains at least one unmasked token.
Run a mixed-precision forward and backward smoke test containing padded sequences before full training.
repairs.root_cause: A mask sentinel chosen for float32 was applied directly to half-precision attention scores, exceeding float16's finite range.
repairs.title: Provisional: use dtype-safe attention mask sentinels under mixed precision
repairs.when_to_use: Use when custom attention pooling for the author classifier runs under AMP and masked_fill raises an at::Half overflow error.

repairs.failure_pattern: Transformer fine-tuning fails during the first epoch with an attempt to backward through a graph a second time while gradient checkpointing and mixed-precision scaling are enabled.
repair_steps: Disable model gradient checkpointing for this training pipeline.
Use a smaller per-device microbatch and gradient accumulation to retain the desired effective batch size.
Ensure each optimizer update is driven by one scaled backward call per microbatch and that no loss tensor from a prior step is retained.
Run a short forward-backward optimizer-step test before starting the full training schedule.
repairs.root_cause: The selected gradient-checkpointing path is incompatible with the loss and AMP backward behavior in this training implementation, causing checkpointed intermediates to be reused after release.
repairs.title: Provisional: disable incompatible gradient checkpointing and reduce microbatch size
repairs.when_to_use: Use when DeBERTa fine-tuning for this task raises a repeated-backward or freed-tensor error only after gradient checkpointing is enabled with AMP.

repairs.failure_pattern: Cross-validation fails on the first fold because XGBoost rejects gpu_hist and reports that only approx, auto, exact, and hist are valid tree methods.
repair_steps: Inspect the installed XGBoost version and its supported tree-method and device parameters before cross-validation.
Use tree_method='hist' for the supported CPU path in this embedding classifier.
Remove incompatible GPU-specific tree-method parameters rather than mixing them with the CPU configuration.
Run a small first-fold training smoke test and confirm early-stopping metadata is available before launching all folds.
Use the resulting best boosting-round count consistently when retraining on the full author-classification data.
repairs.root_cause: The training configuration assumes the legacy gpu_hist method is available, but the installed XGBoost build exposes a different set of tree methods.
repairs.title: Provisional: select an XGBoost tree method supported by the installed build
repairs.when_to_use: Use when XGBoost training over frozen transformer embeddings rejects gpu_hist before producing a fold metric.
